learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 3/4 scoops and locked it in for three cups divided into quarter-cup scoops.
observations.exploration: Baseline one-cup scoop gave three scoops. Half-cup gave six. Quarter-cup gave twelve and unlocked reveal. Fifth-cup gave fifteen. Total rice remained three cups.
observations.reveal: Corrected twelve for the original quarter-cup question. Explains four scoops in each of three cups, division as how many pieces fit, and dividing by 1/n as multiplying by n.
observations.visual: Inspected inline quarter-cup screenshot: three outlined cups each partitioned into four numbered sections, numbered cumulatively through twelve. Labels and scoop presets are legible. Trust count 4/4 was ignored.
observations.isolation: No-history evaluation preview banner present. Visible trust count ignored.
observations.reference: Own CUA tab 543884163 snapshots and inspected inline screenshot; no screenshot file saved.

prediction.reason: Clear everyday measurement question tests division-always-shrinks misconception.
prediction.evidence: Selected 3/4 versus twelve observed quarter-cup sections.

interaction.reason: Several scoop sizes visibly change partition count while preserving total volume.
interaction.evidence: One, half, quarter and fifth cups gave three, six, twelve and fifteen scoops.

payoff.reason: Connects the actual partition to reciprocal multiplication and the size-below-one condition.
payoff.evidence: Four sections per cup times three cups, then 1/n rule.

clarity.reason: Numbered sections, fixed cup count and named scoop choices make the task clear.
clarity.evidence: Quarter-cup screenshot and three successful changes.

transfer.reason: Reusable measurement interpretation and condition are given, without a concrete new application.
transfer.evidence: Pieces smaller than one increase the count; no new total or context.

accessibility.evidence: Keyboard, focus, contrast audit, phone, zoom/reflow and motion unknown.

surprise.reason: Committed fractional answer is overturned by twelve countable sections.

visualExplanation.reason: Cup partitions carry the division mechanism across multiple sizes.
visualExplanation.evidence: Half, quarter and fifth counts plus screenshot.

practicalValue.evidence: Rice measured by cup and scoop size.

depth.reason: Measurement division and reciprocal multiplication are linked.
depth.evidence: Fixed total with several unit fractions.

complexity.reason: One familiar quantity is partitioned into smaller units.

whyCool: Smaller scoops create more numbered pieces without adding any rice.
caveat: Only unit fractions and a fixed three-cup total were tested.
